about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Emilia Strong Sykes

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS HIT THE GROUND RUNNING IN AUGUST
statements.title: CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS HIT THE GROUND RUNNING IN AUGUST
sentences: The cost of healthcare continues to rise, and harmful cuts to Medicaid and Medicare enacted in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act began taking effect this year.

That means that 37,000 residents in our area are seeing higher healthcare costs tied to the end of the enhanced ACA tax credits, while nearly 30,000 people are losing healthcare coverage due to changes in Medicaid and marketplace eligibility rules.
The State of Ohio saw the second highest number of people unenrolled--that means uninsured--because of the cuts to the ACA tax credits.
It is because of Trump's reckless war of choice in Iran.
Yet, here we are: new strikes on Iran with no end in sight.
As the co-leader in the Housing Affordability Working Group, I am leading legislation that lowers housing costs for renters and homeowners alike.
I introduced the HOMES Act, which ends tax breaks for private equity firms buying up houses in Ohio and across the country, making it more difficult for people to find a place to live.

To bring down the cost of healthcare, I am fighting to reinstate the enhanced ACA tax credits and to repeal cuts to Medicaid and Medicare that will throw people off of their healthcare and put our hospitals at risk of closure.

I also voted for the bipartisan Social Security Fairness Act, which has been signed into law, thankfully, because of our previous administration, ensuring that teachers, firefighters, and other public employees receive their full Social Security benefits.
Maybe somebody will play the tape back since no one seems to want to be here for this important discussion, but I am going to go ahead and provide some solutions.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HOME- AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES FRAUD
statements.title: HOME- AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES FRAUD
sentences: As a former State legislator, I served on the finance committee, and I was the ranking member for the health and human services subcommittee that oversaw the funding and activities toward the home-based and community-based services and Medicaid as an entire agency.
To be clear, Ohio Auditor Keith Faber, who was a witness at last week's hearing, does not currently set Medicaid policy, at least not today.
Further, why weren't there any notable flags in the HCBS program in the last State audit of the Department of Medicaid?

In 2013, Ohio created the Joint Medicaid Oversight Committee to strengthen accountability when the State expanded Medicaid under Republican Governor John Kasich, but that committee was dissolved last year by a Republican supermajority in the legislature and signed by the Republican Governor while it was actively reviewing Medicaid administration, including contracts with major claim processors.
The hearing also featured testimony from State Representative Mike Dovilla, who described oversight failures and data fragmentation that he argues persisted for years within Ohio's Medicaid system.

However, what I do not support is using allegations of fraud to mischaracterize an entire program, promote racist and xenophobic ideologies, limit the care of our most vulnerable citizens, or by presenting only part of the story.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
statements.title: NATIONAL GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
sentences: Mr. Speaker, this National Gun Violence Awareness Month, I rise today thinking about families in Ohio's 13th Congressional District, families whose lives were changed forever by gun violence.
Her family now mourns her death by advocating for gun safety programs.
She said something that captures the pain so many families carry after gun violence: ``Losing a child is a different kind of hurt and pain.'' She is right.

Because gun violence leaves permanent scars on families and communities long after the headlines fade, my heart goes out to the Cook family, the Glover family, the Keleman family, the Weems family, and every family in Ohio's 13th Congressional District and across the country who are trying to heal after losing loved ones to senseless and preventable violence.
In my district, Akron police have responded to 562 calls involving shootings or shots fired through the end of April of this year.
But to the people of my district and to the people across America, this threat of living with gun violence every single day, I want to tell you this: It does not have to be this way.

Four years ago, Congress proved progress is possible when we passed the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, the most significant gun safety legislation in decades, because Democrats and Republicans came together to expand background checks, close the dangerous boyfriend loophole, crack down on illegal gun trafficking, invest in mental health services, strengthen school safety, and fund community intervention programs that are saving lives now.

Just weeks ago, the Trump administration announced efforts to roll back key gun safety protections, including weakening enhanced background checks established under the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, rescinding restrictions on stabilizing braces, and repealing the bump stock ban that President Trump himself put into place after the deadly Las Vegas shooting in 2017.
Mr. Speaker, if you talk to any law enforcement agency, they will tell you that guns continue to create a problem for the work that they do every day.

They encourage us to be smarter on gun safety regulations and ensuring that not only are the communities safer but that those who are sworn to protect and serve us can be safe in their communities, as well.
Mr. Speaker, this Gun Violence Awareness Month--

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AGRICULTURE, RURAL DEVELOPMENT, FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION, AND RELATED AGENCY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
statements.title: AGRICULTURE, RURAL DEVELOPMENT, FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION, AND RELATED AGENCY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
sentences: Mr. Chair, I rise in support of my amendment No. 22, which calls on the FDA to require infant formula and toddler food manufacturers to implement an environmental monitoring regime for deadly contaminants like botulism and salmonella.
I urge my colleagues to support this en bloc and to also support my INFANTS Act, which would empower the FDA to take the appropriate action to protect our precious babies.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CHAMPION OF THE WEEK: AKRON MENTAL HEALTH COURT
statements.title: CHAMPION OF THE WEEK: AKRON MENTAL HEALTH COURT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, May is Mental Health Awareness Month, a time for us to stop and consider how mental health impacts and effects everyone in our communities.
For that reason, I am going to recognize the Akron Municipal Mental Health Court as Ohio's 13th Congressional District's Champion of the Week.

Founded by Judge Elinore Marsh Stormer in response to the growing number of people with serious mental illnesses entering into the criminal justice system, the Akron Municipal Mental Health Court became the first of its kind in Ohio, and one of the first in the Nation.
The Akron Municipal Mental Health Court exemplifies the very best of Ohio's 13th Congressional District and reminds us why our community is proudly known as the birthplace of champions.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RELIABLE FEDERAL INFRASTRUCTURE ACT
statements.title: RELIABLE FEDERAL INFRASTRUCTURE ACT
sentences: While Americans across the Nation are struggling to pay for gas, groceries, housing, and healthcare, my colleagues across the aisle believe the most pressing matter for the American people is phasing out clean energy standards for new and renovated Federal buildings.
If they actually did care about my constituents or the American public, they would shift their focus toward the real reason that costs are going up: Trump's tariffs and Trump's war in Iran.
My amendment would prevent the bill from taking effect until the Secretary publishes a certification that the war in Iran has not increased energy and gas prices in the United States.
Although, even if he were to do that, it would show us that the war in Iran is increasing gas prices in the United States, so I am pretty confident that you would not have accepted it either way.
I rise in opposition to H.R. 4690, the Reliable Federal Infrastructure Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TAX DAY
statements.title: TAX DAY
sentences: Republican policies like the One Big Beautiful Bill Act gave massive tax breaks to millionaires, billionaires, and big corporations.
Add in President Trump's lack of strategy on tariffs, which amounts to a national sales tax, and now families are paying more out of pocket while the wealthiest get a permanent tax break.

The one big, ugly bill also slashed a trillion dollars from Medicaid and cut billions to SNAP, jeopardizing healthcare and food for millions of Americans across the country and tens of thousands of my constituents.
Mr. Speaker, we don't need to raise costs on working families to give more tax breaks to the wealthy.
My Lowering Your Taxes Act expands the earned income tax credit and the child tax credit so working families can better afford childcare, groceries, housing, and other expenses.

That effort should be rewarded and not taxed, but because of the carelessly thrown together no tax on overtime provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, thousands of members of organized labor, the very people who built and made this country run, are excluded.
Well, I believe it should be working for the people, for the workers putting in overtime, parents trying to afford childcare, and families choosing between groceries and healthcare.
Working families deserve policies that lower costs and reward hard work and leaders who will fight for them every single day.
At the end of the day, I will never stop advocating for my constituents and for the American public who deserve so much better than this.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: 16TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE AFFORDABLE CARE ACT
statements.title: 16TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE AFFORDABLE CARE ACT
sentences: Madam Speaker, today, I rise on behalf of the families of Ohio's 13th Congressional District as we mark a momentous occasion: the 16th anniversary of the Affordable Care Act, also known as ObamaCare.
For 16 years, the ACA has been a lifeline.
Because of ObamaCare, more than 50 million Americans have gained health coverage, including tens of thousands of my own constituents.
In my district, about 32,000 people currently rely on ACA coverage.
Ninety percent of them depended on the enhanced premium tax credit to make that coverage even more affordable.
The ACA has allowed more than 133 million Americans with preexisting conditions to be protected, and young people can stay on their parents' health insurance until they are 26 years old.
Essential benefits, from prescription drugs to preventive care, are guaranteed.
Democrats worked to strengthen the Affordable Care Act by lowering premiums and putting an average of $2,400 back into the pockets of working families.
On January 1, the Republicans let the enhanced ACA tax credits expire.
Eight out of every 10 people enrolled in the ACA marketplace plans are experiencing higher premiums this year.
For 16 years, Republicans have tried to dismantle ObamaCare and oppose our healthcare reforms, with nothing else to offer.
They tried to take us back to a time when care was out of reach, when people could be denied coverage for preexisting conditions, and when a single diagnosis can mean financial ruin.

Through their big, ugly bill, Republicans cut more than $1 trillion from our healthcare system, gutting marketplaces, driving up premiums, and making it harder for families to get the care that they need, all while prioritizing tax breaks for the wealthiest Americans and corporations.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HUMAN AND ECONOMIC COSTS OF WAR IN IRAN
statements.title: HUMAN AND ECONOMIC COSTS OF WAR IN IRAN
sentences: They are among the 13 who have lost their lives to date after Trump waged war in Iran.
Since President Trump dragged us into this war with Iran, 13 Americans have already died.
Cars, gas, insurance, and public transit costs are becoming increasingly expensive.
Instead, his tariffs, which act like a national sales tax on American families, and the Republicans' big, ugly bill are driving up costs and squeezing families' budgets even more.
Mr. Speaker, I refuse to sit back and watch working families in Ohio get squeezed like this.
The bill would expand the earned income tax credit and child tax credit so working families can keep more of the money that they earn.
Republicans have ignored warning signs and blocked cost-cutting solutions, and they have left working families to fend for themselves.
We can act to restore affordability, or we can keep letting costs spiral while Republicans protect the millionaires and the billionaires.
I introduced the Lower Your Taxes Act to do such a thing.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NORFOLK SOUTHERN TRAIN DERAILMENT
statements.title: NORFOLK SOUTHERN TRAIN DERAILMENT
sentences: That is why this week I am introducing the Railroad Safety and Accountability Act to protect labor and public interest voices in rail safety decisions, voices that Federal regulators have tried to push aside.

As President Trump has pledged, we will ensure that people of East Palestine are not forgotten, and we will use every resource to prevent other communities from enduring what they experienced.'' During a Transportation and Infrastructure hearing last year, I asked Secretary Duffy directly what concrete steps were being taken to stop another derailment like this one.
We deserve a Congress that puts people over profits, and I will keep fighting until that happens. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: 2025 FINAL PRIORITY RESULTS SURVEY
statements.title: 2025 FINAL PRIORITY RESULTS SURVEY
sentences: They wanted me to protect Social Security, Medicaid, and Medicare.
The number one issue by far was protecting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.

They talked about their lives, how Social Security is how they pay their bills; Medicare is how they get healthcare without going broke; and Medicaid is how their kids, their parents, and neighbors with disabilities can get the support and help they need.

I have worked across the aisle to introduce bipartisan legislation to keep Social Security offices open and services running during government shutdowns because seniors shouldn't lose access to help just because Congress can't get its act together.
I have pushed the Social Security Administration to stop clawing back overpayments when the mistakes were not the fault of the seniors.
I introduced legislation to make sure survivors of domestic violence are not punished under Social Security rules for leaving unsafe marriages.
If you have worked your entire life and paid in every paycheck, Congress should keep its promise in its Social Security program.
That is why I have been fighting to extend the ACA's tax credits to lower healthcare costs, especially for our most vulnerable citizens.

Additionally, I introduced legislation to crack down on junk fees that would drain family budgets, and I have worked in a bipartisan manner to lower costs and improve clean water infrastructure in communities that need it the most.

Instead of staying focused on lowering costs, House Republicans have spent too much time protecting tax breaks for millionaires and billionaires, blocking reforms that would help families, and threatening government shutdowns that only add to more chaos.
I would also mention the no tax on overtime that they have so happily touted doesn't really help so many people in organized labor.
I will keep fighting for what the people of Ohio's 13th Congressional District made clear when they sent me here because this Congress does not belong to party leaders or special interests.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RISING HOUSING COSTS
statements.title: RISING HOUSING COSTS
sentences: That means housing costs are often the largest part of a monthly budget, and this is even before groceries, childcare, or healthcare.
With aging homes and data centers driving up the cost of utilities, people are feeling the crunch.
For some families, rising costs lead to housing instability or homelessness.
That is why, last November, I pressed the Department of Housing and Urban Development to protect Federal funding and homelessness prevention programs in Summit and Stark Counties.
Large corporate investors are buying up single-family homes, driving up prices and rents, and locking families out of homeownership.

That is why, last summer, I introduced the HOMES Act, which cracks down on investors buying 50 or more single-family homes, shines a light on corporate ownership and rental practices, and makes sure local families, not profit-seeking investors, get first access to homeownership.
That is why I secured Federal funding for the East Akron Neighborhood Development Corporation to help expand affordable housing, revitalize neighborhoods, and create jobs.

As chair of the New Democrat Coalition's Affordable Housing Task Force, I helped develop a housing action plan with more than 20 recommendations to increase housing supply, reform zoning and permitting, strengthen Federal incentives, grow the construction workforce, and improve transparency.
Homelessness programs that protect our most vulnerable neighbors must be preserved.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CHAMPION OF THE WEEK: CONRAD PIERO
statements.title: CHAMPION OF THE WEEK: CONRAD PIERO
sentences: On December 18, Conrad, a loss prevention specialist at a Walmart in Canton, Ohio, was working in the store when a man being held for allegedly shoplifting pulled a gun on a Canton police officer who was present and attempting to question and detain the suspect.
Both the Canton Police Department and Walmart said that Conrad went above and beyond in his service to our community, and I could not agree more.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RISING HEALTHCARE COSTS
statements.title: RISING HEALTHCARE COSTS
sentences: The enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired December 31, 2025, and now health coverage is more expensive and families are already feeling the impact.
In my district, 90 percent of the 32,000 people who get ACA coverage rely on those subsidies.
In Canton, AultCare, a regional insurer tied to Aultman Hospital, stopped offering some individual family and small business ACA plans before December 31.
These are working families and small business employees losing coverage because Republicans refuse to act.

Republicans also pushed a partisan healthcare bill that would make things much worse by increasing the number of uninsured people, shifting costs onto working families, and weakening the protections that so many Americans rely upon.
I offered an amendment to protect working families from losing health coverage and to protect access to reproductive healthcare.
It is from the Medicaid program that has already been cut by a trillion dollars and the ACA marketplace health plans.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 6703, LOWER HEALTH CARE PREMIUMS FOR ALL AMERICANS ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 498, DO NO HARM IN MEDICAID ACT; PRO
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 6703, LOWER HEALTH CARE PREMIUMS FOR ALL AMERICANS ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 498, DO NO HARM IN MEDICAID ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R...
sentences: This Republican healthcare crisis is completely and entirely preventable, and House Democrats and even a few Republicans have a solution: Extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced premium tax credits.

It is a collection of failed policies that would raise prices, leaving an additional 100,000 people without insurance and restricting access to abortion care, setting the stage for a national abortion ban.
Right now, any and all abortion coverage provided under marketplace plans are not paid for by Federal dollars.
Mr. Speaker, today I rise in support of my proposed amendment to H.R. 6703 and in opposition to the underlying bill.
I urge my colleagues to extend the enhanced tax credits before it is too late.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3898, PROMOTING EFFICIENT REVIEW FOR MODERN INFRASTRUCTURE TODAY ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3383, INCREASING INVES
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3898, PROMOTING EFFICIENT REVIEW FOR MODERN INFRASTRUCTURE TODAY ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3383, INCREASING INVESTOR OPPORTUNITIES ACT; PROVIDING...
sentences: To build on Akron's generations of success, my second amendment requires the Secretary of Defense to establish an initiative to accelerate the research and development of innovative and sustainable polymer processing and manufacturing to support next generation technologies built on a resilient polymer supply chain.
Mr. Speaker, today I rise in support of my proposed amendments to the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal year 2026.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CHAMPIONS OF THE WEEK: NORTH CANTON FIRST RESPONDERS
statements.title: CHAMPIONS OF THE WEEK: NORTH CANTON FIRST RESPONDERS
sentences: In the early hours of October 9, Sergeant Cody Dollinger, Officer Adam Knam, Officer Michael Foltz, and firefighter-paramedic Eli Bosler of the North Canton Police and Fire Departments responded to reports of gunfire and injuries at a local apartment complex.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4312, STUDENT COMPENSATION AND OPPORTUNITY THROUGH RIGHTS AND ENDORSEMENTS ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1005, COMBAT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4312, STUDENT COMPENSATION AND OPPORTUNITY THROUGH RIGHTS AND ENDORSEMENTS ACT; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1005, COMBATING THE LIES OF AUTHORITARIANS IN...
sentences: Mr. Speaker, today I rise in opposition to the rule and H.R. 4312, the SCORE Act.
This legislation fails to address the rights of students to advocate for themselves, and that is why I introduced an amendment to allow for students to collectively bargain.
That is why I introduced an amendment in the Rules Committee to strike the language from the bill and allow students to be properly compensated for their labor.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HIGHER COSTS OF EVERYDAY LIFE
statements.title: HIGHER COSTS OF EVERYDAY LIFE
sentences: When policies put pressure on working families instead of supporting them, the impact shows up in higher bills and tighter budgets.
Aarit aspires to become a lawyer and ultimately land an appointment as a Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
I am committed to supporting the creation of good-paying jobs so families in Ohio's 13th District and all across the country can worry a little less and hope a lot more.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MY AMENDMENTS TO H.R. 3838
statements.title: MY AMENDMENTS TO H.R. 3838
sentences: This amendment, which is based on the Airship Improvement Research for Safety and Humanitarian Innovation Projects Act, or the AIRSHIPS Act, would support the research into additional civilian cases for airships, often referred to as ``blimps,'' that could contribute to national defense; provide economic, sustainable, and clean air cargo transportation; support disaster response efforts; and provide humanitarian aid to people in areas of need.
The Tech Hub aims to advance critical polymer and advanced material innovations of defense, mobility, healthcare, and semiconductor industries.

Strong coordination with the labor units through the Tri-County Labor Council within the region ensures the creation of good-quality jobs for workers from all educational and socioeconomic backgrounds, all with the protections of organized labor.
Last year, the Akron Sustainable Polymers Tech Hub was awarded approximately $51 million in Federal funds, thanks to the historic CHIPS and Science Act.

Mr. Speaker, today I rise in support of my proposed amendments to H.R. 3838, the Streamlining Procurement for Effective Execution and Delivery and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026.

That is why I am introducing this amendment that urges the Department of Defense to collaborate with Tech Hubs to accelerate defense innovations in partnerships with academia and industry right in our backyards.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MASSIVE CUTS TO ENERGY AND WATER INFRASTRUCTURE
statements.title: MASSIVE CUTS TO ENERGY AND WATER INFRASTRUCTURE
sentences: Funding these projects is crucial to ensure my constituents have access to clean water in their homes.

Here is just another example of snatching hard- earned constituents' dollars that they expected to be reinvested in their community, only to be sent elsewhere to pay for billionaire tax cuts or something else nefarious and nothing that anyone asked for.
Mr. Speaker, today, I rise in opposition to the fiscal year 2026 Energy and Water appropriations bill.
For this reason and many others, I urge my colleagues to oppose this bill because it does not lower costs.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SINGLE, UNIQUE ZIP CODES FOR CERTAIN COMMUNITIES
statements.title: SINGLE, UNIQUE ZIP CODES FOR CERTAIN COMMUNITIES
sentences: When ZIP Codes were first assigned for this area, Green was a township, mostly farmland and a few businesses, and fewer than 10,000 residents.
Madam Speaker, today I rise in support of H.R. 3095, a bill that would assign a new ZIP Code to the city of Green, a municipality within Ohio's 13th Congressional District.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: People don't have extra money to pay for billionaires' yachts and monthslong vacations.
This bill takes money away from hardworking Americans and gives it to the rich.
Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today to oppose this terrible bill that is a bad deal for Ohio, the residents of Ohio's 13th Congressional District, and the people of the United States of America.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DOBBS DECISION ANNIVERSARY
statements.title: DOBBS DECISION ANNIVERSARY
sentences: Mr. Speaker, 3 years ago, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, ripping away a constitutional right that generations of women had relied on for nearly one-half century.
What followed was a full-scale assault on reproductive healthcare: abortion, contraception, IVF, and even access to emergency care.

Just hours after the Dobbs decision was handed down, an extreme and deeply unpopular 6-week abortion ban went into effect, essentially outlawing abortion before many people even knew they are pregnant.

In November 2023, Ohioans from across the political spectrum came together and voted to enshrine reproductive freedom directly into our State's constitution: the ability to bear a child, to use contraception, and to access abortion care.
This dangerous bill would ban nearly all abortions in Ohio, criminalize doctors, and potentially treat patients seeking care as criminals.
Under this proposal, abortion could be prosecuted as homicide.
The United States Supreme Court's recent decision in Moyle v. United States dismissed an opportunity to affirm that emergency abortion care is protected under Federal law.
That is why I introduced a resolution to reaffirm access to emergency care and abortion care to all Americans.
That is why House Democrats have introduced bills to guarantee abortion rights across the country and protect access to birth control, IVF, and other fertility care.
As a Representative of Ohio's 13th Congressional District, I will keep standing up for our freedom, and I will keep working to ensure our laws reflect our values.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: OBSERVING GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
statements.title: OBSERVING GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
sentences: Mr. Speaker, gun violence is a scourge that has plagued the United States for far too long.
We have a duty as public servants to keep our communities safe, but the inaction on gun violence is killing innocent Americans.
We can and must pass commonsense gun safety legislation to bolster background checks and ban dangerous assault weapons.
The people of Ohio's 13th Congressional District sent me here to do something about gun violence in our communities, and that is exactly what I intend to do.
This is Gun Violence Awareness Month.
This month, and every other day, I mourn the lives of the countless people who have lost their lives to senseless gun violence and those whom they have left behind. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2483, SUPPORT FOR PATIENTS AND COMMUNITIES REAUTHORIZATION ACT OF 2025; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2931, SAVE SBA FROM
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2483, SUPPORT FOR PATIENTS AND COMMUNITIES REAUTHORIZATION ACT OF 2025; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2931, SAVE SBA FROM SANCTUARY CITIES ACT OF 2025...
sentences: Mr. Speaker, today, I rise to talk about an issue that touches every community in this country, mental health.
We have only about half of the mental health behavioral workforce that we need to meet the demand.

It also includes my bipartisan legislation, the Mental Health Improvement Act, which provides tens of millions of dollars annually to expand our behavioral health workforce, helping to train, recruit, and retain mental health professionals across the country.
In a meeting with the behavioral health services there, they said they don't have enough people to work for the need that is in our community.
This is unacceptable, undermining the Medicaid program and getting people kicked off.
We need to put programs in place that will help our citizens, save lives, and keep our communities safe.
That is why I urge my colleagues to not only pass this bipartisan legislation but also to continue to advocate for its implementation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EARTHQUAKER DEVICES SOUNDS THE ALARM
statements.title: EARTHQUAKER DEVICES SOUNDS THE ALARM
sentences: EarthQuaker Devices employs 34 workers and offers premium health insurance, paid sick leave, a 401(k) match, and competitive wages.
It is because of reckless tariff policies.
The President's tariffs have increased their cost of goods by $500,000.
Does the government truly not understand the impact of their actions, or is it their goal to destroy us?'' She goes on to say: ``For the first time, I am considering offshoring our manufacturing.
The President's tariff policy, which he alleges is meant to drive domestic innovation and manufacturing, is causing a small but mighty business in Akron to consider offshoring their manufacturing.
Tariffs are a useful tool to level the playing field, and, when properly implemented, they can create jobs and spur manufacturing.
As someone from northeast Ohio, I have seen the consequences of bad trade deals and the impact of NAFTA.
This country slapped tariffs on our allies.
If our goal is to stop offshoring and revitalize American manufacturing, why are we punishing the companies that are driving innovation, the ones who are footing the bill?
To lower costs, let's go after the price-gouging billionaires and corporate monopolies, not small business owners keeping our communities alive.
Mr. Speaker, I urge this body to listen to the voices of our constituents like Julie.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: I have said many times before that access to maternal health, to infant mortality reduction, to making sure that people have access to substance and mental health services is what is so important.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
statements.title: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
sentences: For Mariah and her daughter, Medicaid is a crucial resource without which they would not be able to afford the proper care that her daughter requires for her condition.
In her message to my office, Mariah said: ``I am asking for the budget to not touch Medicaid funding.

I would be lost without all of these resources for her.'' Mariah's story is one of heroism, but not different than many of my other constituents', a mother working hard to provide for her daughter who was born and lives with a condition that requires the care that Medicaid provides.
Thousands of constituents from Ohio's 13th Congressional District have called and written to my offices in Akron, Canton, and here in D.C., imploring me to save Medicaid.
That is exactly what I am going to do.
I am going to fight for Mariah and Ohio's 13th Congressional District. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MENTAL HEALTH SOLUTIONS
statements.title: MENTAL HEALTH SOLUTIONS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to speak about an issue that touches every community in this country: mental health.
More than one in five adults in the United States live with a mental health illness.
In Ohio, we have seen just how urgent this crisis has become, where we have only about half the behavioral health workforce we need to meet the demand.

That is why I have reintroduced the Mental Health Improvement Act, a bipartisan bill to provide tens of millions of dollars annually to expand our behavioral health workforce, helping to train, recruit, and retain mental health professionals across the country.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SOCIAL SECURITY ADMINISTRATION IS THERE TO HELP, NOT HURT, AMERICANS
statements.title: SOCIAL SECURITY ADMINISTRATION IS THERE TO HELP, NOT HURT, AMERICANS
sentences: On January 5, President Biden signed the Social Security Fairness Act into law, expanding Social Security for thousands of Americans whose benefits, that they earned through years of hard work, were cut because of bad policies.
The Social Security Fairness Act is estimated to result in an average increase of $360 per month for more than 2.5 million Social Security recipients, according to the Congressional Budget Office.
I have heard from countless people in my community, they are thrilled that they were finally able to get the Social Security benefit that they deserve and earned.

There wasn't anywhere that I could go in the community: church, the grocery store, the gym, restaurants, someone always stopped me to thank me for voting for the Social Security Fairness Act and to tell me a story of how it is going to change lives.
You can imagine my disappointment as the Social Security Administration has taken recent actions to hurt, not help, the American people, including those in Ohio's 13th.

From cutting phone helplines, to requiring certain services be conducted in person, to slowing down processing times, and closing offices, the American people are not getting the service they earned from the Social Security Administration.
Now, to add insult to injury, the Trump administration is vowing to withhold the benefits of Americans as a result of mistakes made by the Social Security Administration.
Instead of making the Social Security Administration work better and remain solvent, the Trump administration is accusing seniors of fraud and calling their earned benefits waste.
The fraud is an unelected billionaire, the richest man in the world, who is cutting services to low- and middle-income families.

Our seniors rely on Social Security to pay their bills, to put food on their tables, to keep a roof over their head, and if the Social Security Administration makes a mistake, it can be addressed in time.
With more than 97,000 residents of my district living under the poverty line and 175,000 residents relying on Social Security, these payments are, in fact, a lifeline.
I have already heard from constituents who have been contacted by the Social Security Administration who are concerned about the changes and the cuts.
These overpayments were as a result of a mistake by the Social Security Administration and not the fault of my constituents.
Changes to the Social Security Administration that prevent beneficiaries from accessing their full benefits are nothing more than backdoor benefit cuts, and I will not stand for it.
We already know that this is just a setup for cuts, and these changes are setups to pay for tax giveaways for the richest, the billionaires, and greedy corporations.

I ask you and all of my colleagues who I serve with to make sure that we protect Social Security, keep it solvent, and ensure that we are protecting the benefits that they have earned for hard work over several years and decades of service. ____________________
I will always stand in the way of these wolf-in-sheep's-clothing policies.
